summary: Meta: set the advertiser flags from the ATT answer, not from each app
description:
MT-1193 found that Ereasy, Photo up and Video up each hardcode Facebook's isAdvertiserIDCollectionEnabled to true, whatever the user answered to the tracking prompt. The conclusion on that ticket, following Meta's own guidance, is that the flag should track the ATT decision - collection on when the user allowed tracking, off when they did not - together with isAdvertiserTrackingEnabled for the versions where that still has an effect. All three apps are now fixing it individually.

MartechKit sets neither flag. Neither name appears anywhere in the package, and there is no Meta phase-2 hook, so the Meta module is never told what the user answered - TikTok is the only module that receives the ATT outcome today.

That leaves each app to do it, and the way MT-1193 records them doing it is by calling ATTrackingManager.requestTrackingAuthorization in the app. MartechKit owns that call: host apps are told not to make it, and Martech.requestATT() is meant to be the only place it happens. An app that follows MT-1193 and integrates MartechKit ends up with two paths to the same prompt.

This is the kind of vendor rule the package exists to absorb: decided once, applied the same way in every app, instead of three teams each getting it right separately.

On iOS 17 with Facebook SDK 17 or later, Meta reads the ATT status directly and the tracking setter is deprecated, so the visible behaviour there will not change much. The flags still matter for older versions, for the console warnings, and for the package saying one consistent thing about consent.

Acceptance criteria:
- MartechKit sets Meta's advertiser ID collection flag from the user's ATT answer rather than leaving it to the host app
- The Meta module is told the ATT outcome, as the TikTok module already is
- The advertiser tracking flag is handled for the versions where it still has an effect
- An app integrating MartechKit needs neither to call ATT itself nor to set either flag in order to be correct
- The behaviour is documented, including what apps that set these flags themselves today should remove
- Tests cover both ATT answers
- The three apps in MT-1193 are told whether to keep their local fix or drop it once they move to a version of the SDK that does this
